en.title: Alloy Production
en.description:
Each unit of alloy needs composition[i] units of metal i; you already have stock[i] and can buy more at a unit price of cost[i], with a budget of budget. Find the maximum number of units you can produce.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n budget; the next three lines are composition, stock, and cost respectively. Constraints added by this site: 1≤n≤100000, 0≤budget≤10^9, 1≤composition[i],cost[i]≤10^9, 0≤stock[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output the maximum number of alloy units.
en.explanation: The purchase cost for an output of x is Σmax(0,x·composition[i]−stock[i])·cost[i], which is non-decreasing in x, so binary search for the largest feasible output. The source's example output of 1 is correct, but the cost formula in the original explanation is wrong; this site corrects it according to the rules.
